platformMapping.units: Token px = dp on Android, pt on iOS. Type sizes = sp (Android font scale) / pt scaled with Dynamic Type via Font.custom(relativeTo:) and @ScaledMetric. Hold 1.3x without clipping.
platformMapping.schemes: Android: MilkrunTheme(scheme) -> Kraft (light) / Night (isSystemInDarkTheme) / Sun (header toggle), exposed via LocalMilkrunColors and mapped onto Material 3 roles. iOS: an Environment value carrying the same role set; Kraft/Night follow colorScheme, Sun is the same app toggle.
platformMapping.font: Bundle design/fonts/BigShouldersStencilDisplay.ttf (OFL). Android res/font/big_shoulders_stencil with FontVariation weight 700/800. iOS: UIAppFonts in Info.plist; select weight via variation axis 700/800.
platformMapping.icons: Material icons (WbSunny, ArrowBack, QrCodeScanner, Check) on Android; SF Symbols (sun.max / sun.max.fill, chevron.backward, qrcode.viewfinder, checkmark) on iOS.
platformMapping.sheet: Android ModalBottomSheet, label container, 0 corner. iOS .sheet with presentationCornerRadius(0) and label background.

motion.name: tape-on
motion.value: slide in from trailing edge 200ms + fade in 120ms
motion.purpose: Tape tab laid on when a change is recorded.

motion.name: tape-off
motion.value: slide toward leading edge by half width 180ms + fade out 180ms
motion.purpose: Tape tab peels off when the server confirms.

motion.name: reduced
motion.value: crossfade 150ms (tape); sticker and tag appear flat with no scale or tilt
motion.purpose: Reduce Motion replacement for all three.

motion.name: list
motion.value: platform item placement animation (Compose animateItem; SwiftUI default list transitions)
motion.purpose: Rows and stickers moving between sections.

geometry.name: tape-grain
geometry.value: 1.5px lines of on-tape at 10% every 9px (device pixels in the Android build)

geometry.name: torn-ends
geometry.value: six teeth per end, 5px depth (device pixels in the Android build)

geometry.name: stencil-mark
geometry.value: stroke 16% of size, butt caps, 7% bridge gaps
geometry.purpose: Check and cross for finished rows.

geometry.name: marker-strike
geometry.value: 6 wide, round caps, from 62% to 38% of height

narrative.overview:
A route is a stack of boxes to move, so every screen speaks the marks a packing room already uses: corrugated kraft as the ground, near-black stencil ink, label-white stock for the thing in hand, translucent amber packing tape for work the server has not confirmed, safety-orange exception stickers for the server's rulings, and a thick marker strike for a stop dispatch cancelled. Nothing is decorative; each material carries exactly one meaning, and each state has its own physical mark so nothing depends on color alone.

The system is built for a driver mid-shift: one hand busy, sometimes gloved, in direct sun or a dark garage. That sets the density. Type never drops below 15 (body) on arm's-length surfaces, actions are 56 to 64 tall, and the screen has one thing at full strength (the next stop, or on a stop the Deliver block) while everything else recedes by size and ink. The world deliberately refuses the category default of white list cells with colored status chips.

One world, three schemes. **Kraft** is the day scheme, **Night** the dark scheme for garages and dusk (follows the system dark setting), **Sun** a black-on-white maximum-contrast scheme the driver toggles from the route header for direct sunlight. Platform structure stays native (Material 3 on Android, HIG on iOS); the world is applied through each platform's open theming layer.

**Units.** Token dimensions are written as `px` for tooling. Read 1px as 1dp on Android and 1pt on iOS. Type sizes are sp on Android and scale with font scale; on iOS they map to points and must scale with Dynamic Type (use `Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:)` and `@ScaledMetric`). Both platforms must hold 1.3x without clipping.
keyCharacteristics: Kraft ground, stencil ink, label stock; materials, not cards.
Stencil numerals are the headline of every stop; everything else is the platform sans.
Square corners everywhere except die-cut stickers.
Tape means waiting, orange means a ruling, a marker strike means cancelled; each also carries words or a mark.
One lifted label per route view; the rest recedes.
One ink-filled block per screen, isolated from reversible actions.

rules.name: The Tape Is Waiting Rule
rules.body: Amber tape means work recorded on the phone and not yet confirmed by the server, and nothing else. Waiting is calm: tape is never paired with error language, red, or alarm motion.

rules.name: The Orange Is a Ruling Rule
rules.body: Safety orange appears only when the server ruled on something (or a delivery stood over an unseen cancel). It always carries the hazard mark and a plain sentence saying what happened and what to do.

rules.name: The Faded Stencil Rule
rules.body: `*-done-number` is for 28-and-up stencil numerals and stencil marks only. Text that must be read at body size on a finished row uses `*-ink-2`.

rules.name: The Stencil Is For Numbers Rule
rules.body: The stencil face sets stop numbers and the remaining count, nothing else: no words, no headings, no buttons.

rules.name: The Fifteen Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing a driver reads as a sentence is below 15; 13 is reserved for short labels and ids.

rules.name: The One Lifted Label Rule
rules.body: On the route, exactly one stop is on label stock: the next one. Every other stop is a kraft row.

rules.name: The Thumb's Slip Rule
rules.body: The irreversible Deliver never sits within a thumb's slip of another control: 32 of empty space above it, and nothing beside it.

rules.name: The Only Label Lifts Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to label stock. Kraft rows, tape, stickers and buttons are flat.

rules.name: The Fluting Rule
rules.body: The 1-unit fluting line is the system's only divider: between rows, under the done heading, between parcels, and as the "All sent" line. Outlines on controls and the box seam under the tape strip are part of those marks, not dividers.

dos: Do set stop numbers and the remaining count in Big Shoulders Stencil Display and everything else in the platform sans.
Do keep exactly one stop on label stock on the route screen, and step the rest down: 40 stencil in secondary ink for upcoming, 28 faded stencil with a stencil check or cross for finished.
Do give every state its own mark and words: tape tab "Unsent", hazard mark on orange, stencil check or cross, marker strike, and the status line.
Do keep the primary action at 64 and every mid-stop action at 56; chrome at the platform minimum (48 dp / 44 pt).
Do leave 32 of empty space above Deliver.
Do show selection as a heavier frame (4) plus a check.
Do ship all three schemes for every new surface, and give label stock the 2 ink edge in Sun.
Do honour Reduce Motion: tape becomes a 150 ms crossfade, stickers lose their scale and tilt.
Do take every sentence from the shared `Copy` so both apps say the same thing.
donts: Don't use amber tape for anything but unconfirmed work, or orange for anything but a server ruling.
Don't fill a second block with ink on the same screen; the filled block is that screen's primary action alone.
Don't round corners on labels, buttons, fields, sheets or blocks; only stickers are die-cut.
Don't add dividers other than the 1-unit fluting line, and never run the tape seam through text.
Don't put shadows on kraft rows, tape, stickers or buttons.
Don't set words in the stencil face, or set body text in faded stencil.
Don't repeat the stop number as a title in the stop bar.
Don't fall back to white list cells with colored status chips.
Don't imitate Amazon's branding, trade dress or app UI.
